openrouter-for-copilot.config.title: OpenRouter for Copilot
openrouter-for-copilot.config.baseUrl.de: Optional API base URL override. When non-empty, overrides the default OpenRouter endpoint (`https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`). Leave empty to use OpenRouter.
Maximum number of output tokens per request. Set to 0 to use the API default. Useful for controlling costs.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.experiment:
**Experimental**: improve context-cache hit rate by pre-activating available tools.
- When the enabled tools list changes across turns, this may improve context-cache hit rate.
- Requests will include more function definitions, so input tokens may increase. Cache-hit input tokens are billed at a lower price, but still count toward usage.
- This may add internal preflight tool calls to the current Copilot chat history. If you switch to another model in the same conversation, that model provider may reject or mishandle the replayed history. Start a new chat if model switching behaves unexpectedly.

Use [Configure Tools](command:workbench.action.chat.configureTools) to **view and manage** your tool list:

- 64 or fewer enabled tools: usually no need to enable this unless the tool list still changes across turns.
- More than 128 enabled tools: not recommended. The API supports at most 128 functions in one `tools` request. Consider disabling tools you rarely use.
Controls what diagnostic information OpenRouter for Copilot writes. Token usage is always reported to Copilot when the API returns it.

- **Minimal** - Token usage only. No diagnostic logs or request dumps.
- **Metadata** - Privacy-safe diagnostic metadata (request hashes, prefix overlap, tool schema changes). Does not contain prompt text. View with [`OpenRouter: Show Logs`](command:openrouter-for-copilot.showLogs).
- **Verbose** - Complete request payloads written to disk for local debugging. **Warning: contains sensitive prompt content.** View with [`OpenRouter: Open Request Dumps Folder`](command:openrouter-for-copilot.openRequestDumpsFolder).
Token usage only. No diagnostic logs or dumps.
Privacy-safe metadata. Safe to share publicly. View with `OpenRouter: Show Logs`.
Contains sensitive prompt content. For local debugging only.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.ponytailMo: Injects a lazy-senior-dev system instruction before each request. The model is asked to verify the need for code, check the codebase/stdlib/dependencies, and prefer deletion over addition.
No extra instruction. The model follows its default behavior.
Gentle reminder to reuse existing code and avoid unnecessary dependencies.
Full Ponytail ladder: YAGNI â codebase â stdlib â platform â dependencies â one-liner â minimum code. Default.
Aggressive minimalism. Question over-engineering and justify every character.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.codeSimpli: Enable the Code Simplifier autonomous refinement agent (on by default). The model proactively reviews recently modified code and simplifies it for clarity, consistency, and maintainability â reducing nesting, improving naming, and eliminating redundancy while preserving all original behaviour. When enabled, Ponytail is automatically lowered to Lite for compatibility.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.stripThink: Strip leaked reasoning tags ( MÃ¼d, `<ground>`, `<deliberation>`) from model output. Some models leak these into content instead of routing them through the thinking channel.
Strip think tags only for models known to leak them (MiniMax M2 family).
Strip think tags for all models.
Never strip think tags â show raw model output.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.modelIdOve: Override the API model ID sent for any built-in or custom model. Defaults map Copilot utility aliases to OpenRouter slugs; add keys when your endpoint expects a different model name.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.customMode: Additional OpenRouter-compatible models shown in the Copilot model picker. Use either an OpenRouter slug string or an object with `id`, optional display `name`, token limits, `toolCalling`, `thinking`, and `imageInput`. Custom model IDs override built-in IDs in the picker and lookup. Unknown slugs default to Vision Proxy (`imageInput: false`); set `imageInput: true` for native image input.
Custom model ID. Defaults are applied for name, token limits, tool calling, thinking, and image input (Vision Proxy unless `imageInput` is set on an object).
Model ID shown in VS Code and used for requests unless `modelIdOverrides` maps it to another API model ID.
Display name. Defaults to the model ID.
Maximum input tokens shown to Copilot. Defaults to 200000.
Maximum output tokens shown to Copilot. Defaults to 131072.
Whether this custom model supports tool calling. Defaults to true.
Whether this custom model supports thinking mode. Defaults to true.
Whether this custom model accepts native image input. Defaults to false (images go through the Vision Proxy unless `visionMode` is native or mcp).
openrouter-for-copilot.config.visionMode: Compatibility setting managed by [Configure Vision Proxy](command:openrouter-for-copilot.setVisionModel). Stores the selected VS Code vision model as `vendor/id` when that source is active. In automatic mode, an OpenRouter vision model is tried first and this VS Code model is used as fallback.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.visionProm:
Prompt sent to the vision proxy model when describing image attachments before forwarding them to a text-only chat model.

[Configure Vision Proxy](command:openrouter-for-copilot.setVisionModel)
openrouter-for-copilot.config.visionMode:
How image attachments reach the selected chat model.

- **Auto** (default): native when the OpenRouter catalog says the model accepts images, otherwise proxy.
- **Native**: resize and send image bytes directly (2.5 MiB binary budget).
- **Proxy**: a vision model describes the image as text, then the selected model receives that text.
- **MCP**: store images locally and leave a file-path prompt for an image-capable MCP tool.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.imageHandl: System instruction used in `mcp` vision mode. Injected on every mcp-mode turn (including text-only turns) so the prompt-cache prefix stays stable.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.imageStore: Per-image prompt when an attachment is stored as a local file. Placeholders: `{0}` = label, `{1}` = file path.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.mcp.imageC: How locally stored MCP-vision images are cleaned up. **Manual**: keep until [Clean Up Stored Images](command:openrouter-for-copilot.cleanupStoredImages). **7-day TTL**: delete files whose last-referenced time is older than 7 days on activation.

Exact runtime tool IDs to treat as image readers in `mcp` vision mode. Official tools are also detected from a required local-image-path input schema. If no reader is available, the request falls back to the vision proxy when configured.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.agentRoles: Models used by the pipeline's agent roles: research (parallel research step) and review (final code review).
Models used for the parallel research step. Areas are assigned round-robin across the listed models, so multiple models run research concurrently.
Models used for the final code review step.

Models tried in order after the chat-selected implementer is unavailable (e.g. provider outage, quota exhausted). When unset, the audited free models are used as a default safety net — out-of-the-box users get fallback with zero config.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.rules.desc: User-defined rules, injected as a `### USER RULES` block at the top of the system message for every coding request (main-agent and background). Each entry becomes one bullet — use them to enforce project conventions like `Always use TypeScript rather than JavaScript`, `Keep responses concise`, or `Return curly braces on the next line`. Rules are stripped entirely on utility requests (chat-title, git-commit, etc.) so they don't pollute the prompt cache. Empty / whitespace-only entries are dropped automatically.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.allowExtra:
**Experimental:** let the agent swarm call tools beyond its curated whitelist.

By default, research / review / implement agents only see the curated set of built-in VS Code tools (read_file, apply_patch, runTests, …). This keeps prompts small and under the 128-tool cap. When enabled, MCP-discovered tools and other Copilot-registered external tools the user has set up are also forwarded to the agents — useful for database, browser, or ticketing MCP servers.

- Off (default): only curated built-in tools reach the swarm.
- On: curated tools first, then extras appended after them. The 128-tool hard cap still applies; curated tools are always kept before extras when the list is truncated.

Read-only extras are also pulled into the research / review pool when their name looks read-only (`read`, `query`, `search`, `list`, `fetch`, `get`, `resolve`, `describe`). Mutators stay in the implementer pool only.
openrouter-for-copilot.config.auditFreeM:
Per-model probe timeout (milliseconds) for the agent swarm's free-tier audit. When `openrouter-for-copilot.agentRoles` is NOT set, each `@swarm` run starts by probing every OpenRouter `:free` model in parallel and ranking the responders by latency; this setting bounds a single probe. The audit's wall-clock is the *slowest* probe (all probes run in parallel), so the audit adds at most this much to the start of each run.

Default 6000ms (6s). Tune down on slow connections to truncate the audit — if a probe doesn't complete in time, the model is marked ✗(`timeout`) and the swarm routes through the rest. Minimum 500ms, maximum 30000ms. The audit is skipped entirely when you pin `agentRoles.*`, in which case this setting has no effect.
